female.trajectory_modulation: Female sex strongly increases SLE incidence and flare frequency, especially during reproductive years

male.trajectory_modulation: Less common but tends toward more severe phenotype with renal/serositis

african_ancestry.trajectory_modulation: Higher prevalence, earlier onset, more proliferative nephritis, worse renal outcomes

east_asian_ancestry.trajectory_modulation: Increased nephritis risk; multitarget tacrolimus/MMF widely used

pediatric_under_15.trajectory_modulation: Less common but more severe phenotype with frequent nephritis and MAS

late_onset_over_50.trajectory_modulation: More serositis and pulmonary, less nephritis; consider drug-induced SLE

high_recent_uv_exposure.trajectory_modulation: Triggers flare via apoptotic keratinocytes and IFN activation

ebv_or_cmv_recent_activation.trajectory_modulation: Viral mimicry and IFN activation may precipitate flares

covid19_recent.trajectory_modulation: Reported triggering of de novo SLE and flares

pregnancy_or_postpartum.trajectory_modulation: Flare risk increases especially if active disease at conception or HCQ stopped; renal flares disproportionately common

non_adherent_or_recent_discontinuation.trajectory_modulation: HCQ withdrawal is one of the strongest immediate flare risks

current_smoker.trajectory_modulation: Increased cutaneous flares, reduced HCQ efficacy, more thrombosis

hydralazine_procainamide_minocycline_tnf.trajectory_modulation: Drug-induced SLE phenotype (anti-histone, less renal/CNS); discontinue trigger

c1q_c2_c4_deficiency.trajectory_modulation: C1q deficiency near-uniformly causes severe early-onset SLE; C4 null haplotypes increase risk

high_acute_stress.trajectory_modulation: Reported as flare trigger in surveys; mechanistic link via HPA-immune axis

established_ckd_from_prior_nephritis.trajectory_modulation: Predicts worse renal outcomes and complicates flare management

supportive_care: Photoprotection: broad-spectrum SPF50+ sunscreen, sun-protective clothing, UV avoidance
Smoking cessation counseling and support (smoking reduces HCQ efficacy and accelerates atherosclerosis)
Cardiovascular risk reduction: statin if dyslipidemic, lifestyle, BP target <130/80 with proteinuria
Aggressive RAAS blockade for proteinuria with monitoring of K and creatinine

Pneumococcal (PCV13/PCV15 + PPSV23), influenza (annual), HBV, HPV vaccines (live vaccines avoided on biologics/high-dose steroids); recombinant zoster vaccine especially with anifrolumab/JAKi/rituximab
PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX, atovaquone, or dapsone) for prolonged high-dose steroids, CYC, rituximab, severe lymphopenia
TB and HBV/HCV screening before high-intensity immunosuppression and biologics
Bone protection: calcium, vitamin D, baseline DEXA, bisphosphonate for high cumulative steroid exposure
Mental health support and screening for depression and anxiety; acknowledge fatigue impact

Pregnancy planning: ensure quiescent disease 6 months prior, switch teratogens (MMF, CYC, MTX) to azathioprine/tacrolimus/HCQ; aspirin from 12 weeks if APS or risk factors; consider LMWH if APS with prior thrombosis
Contraception counseling: avoid combined estrogen contraceptives if APS-positive or severe disease; progestin or IUD options
Steroid stewardship: target prednisone <=5 mg/day or off; aggressive use of steroid-sparing agents
Glycemic monitoring during steroid therapy; insulin if needed
Ophthalmologic screening for HCQ retinal toxicity (baseline, annual after 5 years; weight-based dosing)
Patient education on flare warning signs, HCQ adherence, and rapid contact pathway
Multidisciplinary care: rheumatology, nephrology for renal flares, dermatology for cutaneous, neurology/psychiatry for NPSLE, obstetrics for pregnancy, hematology for severe cytopenia/APS
